scenes.tagline: Sell what you make to buyers anywhere. Get paid in dollars the moment they buy.
scenes.tag: Stellar Buildathon · Builder's Circle · Nigeria and Ghana
scenes.vo: This is Paperstall: a creator store for Nigeria and Ghana. Sell what you make to buyers anywhere, and get paid in dollars on Stellar the moment they buy.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.head:
Ada sells drum kits to producers abroad.
Getting paid is the hard part.

bullets.v: Payouts wait for processing and stall at weekends.
Sales to buyers abroad lose value when converted to naira.
Her co-producer's share is a bank transfer she sends by hand.

scenes.vo: Meet Ada, a beat-maker in Lagos. She sells drum kits to producers abroad. Selling is easy. Getting paid is not: payouts wait for processing and stall at weekends, foreign sales lose value when they turn into naira, and her co-producer's share is a transfer she sends by hand.

scenes.label: The market and the gap
scenes.head:
Creators already earn here.
The payment rails are missing.

bullets.v: paid out by Selar to its creators in 2025 (Intelpoint).
Listing and selling digital products.
Instant dollar settlement, buyers anywhere, splits that pay themselves.
Circle's USDC on Stellar, passkey smart wallets, fee sponsorship.

scenes.vo: The demand is proven: Selar paid its creators eighteen billion naira in 2025. Listing and selling are solved. Settlement is not: instant dollars, buyers anywhere, splits that pay themselves. Stellar now has all three pieces: Circle's dollar, passkey smart wallets, and fees a store can pay for its users.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.head:
One payment pays everyone,
in the same transaction.

boxes.title: Buyer
boxes.sub: pays in USDC with a passkey

boxes.title: Store contract
boxes.sub: Soroban: splits every sale at once

diagram.note: The receipt on chain unlocks the download. Nobody holds anyone's money.

scenes.vo: One payment does it all. The buyer pays in USDC. A Soroban contract splits it in the same transaction: the creator, up to five co-creators, the affiliate who sent the buyer, and the store's five percent. The receipt on chain unlocks the download.

bullets.v: The buyer pays in USDC with a passkey or any Stellar wallet.
The contract pays the creator, co-creators, affiliate and the 5% fee at once.
The sale on chain is the receipt the server checks before serving the file.

scenes.head: Live on Stellar testnet
scenes.sub: A shelf of real products, each one listed by a creator with a passkey.
scenes.vo: This is Paperstall, live on Stellar testnet. Six aisles, from templates and ebooks to beats and design assets. Every product on the shelf was listed by a creator with a passkey.

scenes.head: List a product with a fingerprint
scenes.sub: No seed phrase, no app, no XLM. The co-designer's 20% is fixed at listing.
scenes.vo: A creator signs in with a fingerprint: no seed phrase, no app, no XLM. They upload the file, set a price in dollars, give a co-designer twenty percent, and sign. The store pays the network fee.

scenes.head: See where the money goes before you pay
scenes.sub: The split on the page is read from the contract.
scenes.vo: Every product page shows where the buyer's four dollars go before anyone pays, read from the contract itself.

scenes.head: Pay with a passkey, download at once
scenes.sub: A new wallet, ten test dollars from the faucet, one tap. The receipt is on chain.
scenes.vo: A buyer abroad pays the same way. A fingerprint makes a wallet, the faucet adds ten test dollars, and one tap pays. The receipt lands on chain and the download unlocks.

scenes.head: The sale on Stellar's explorer
scenes.sub: One buy call on the store contract: 4 USDC for product 30. The 0.04 XLM fee came from the store's sponsor.
scenes.vo: Here is that sale on Stellar's explorer: one call to the store contract, four dollars for product thirty. The network fee came from the store's sponsor account, not the buyer.

scenes.head: Sales land in the creator's wallet
scenes.sub: Every sale with its transaction, and the balance in naira and cedis.
scenes.vo: The creator sees each sale arrive with its transaction, and the balance in naira and cedis at today's rate. No payout to request: the money is already in their wallet.

scenes.head: Cash out through a wallet you own
scenes.sub: Checked on Stellar before saving: the account exists and holds USDC. Then one tap.
scenes.vo: Cash-out stays honest. No Stellar anchor pays naira to a passkey wallet yet, so the creator saves a wallet they own. Paperstall checks it can hold USDC, then sends in one tap. From there, Busha pays naira and MoneyGram pays cedis.

scenes.head: Tested on the live site
scenes.sub: 33 checks with real testnet transactions. The run on 16 Nov 2026 passed all 33.
scenes.vo: Every claim here is tested on the live site: thirty-three checks with real testnet transactions, from the fingerprint sign-up to the payout. The latest run passed all of them, and no passkey wallet ever held XLM.

scenes.label: Why Stellar
scenes.head:
Dollars, speed and wallets
anyone can use, on one network.

bullets.v: issued natively on Stellar
a sale settles before the page reloads
network fee for a sale, paid by the store
the wallet contract checks WebAuthn signatures

scenes.vo: Why Stellar? Circle issues USDC here natively. Ledgers close every five seconds. A sale costs the store under five hundredths of an XLM in fees. And Soroban contract wallets check passkey signatures on chain, so buyers need no crypto at all.

scenes.label: Built on
scenes.head: Every piece is load-bearing.

bullets.v: lists, splits, records receipts
through its asset contract
passkey wallets, smart-account-kit
Freighter, LOBSTR, xBull, Albedo
relayed calls and fee bumps
anchor sign-in, withdrawal, memo IDs

scenes.vo: It is built on a Soroban contract, Circle's USDC, OpenZeppelin smart accounts, Stellar Wallets Kit, fee sponsorship, and the anchor standards for sign-in, withdrawal and exchange memos. Every piece is load-bearing.

scenes.label: Revenue and traction
scenes.head:
A cut of each sale,
taken by the contract.

bullets.v: 5% of every sale on testnet, capped at 10% by the contract, paid in the same transaction.
Affiliates earn a share of the sales they bring, so a creator's audience sells for them.
Live store and demo shop on testnet, 33 of 33 live checks, open source under MIT.

scenes.vo: The business is a cut of each sale, taken by the contract at checkout: five percent today, capped at ten. Affiliates earn a share of the sales they bring. Traction so far: a live store on testnet, a demo shop, thirty-three of thirty-three live checks, and every line open source.

scenes.label: Fit and ecosystem
scenes.head:
Three of the buildathon's focus areas,
in one product.

boxes.title: Paperstall on Stellar
boxes.sub: a store anyone can pay into

diagram.note: Every sale brings a buyer and a creator into USDC on Stellar.

scenes.vo: Paperstall uses three of the buildathon's focus areas at once: stablecoin payments, passkey smart wallets, and Soroban contracts. For Stellar, it brings buyers and creators who have never held crypto into USDC, and a queue of creators ready for the first naira anchor that accepts smart wallets.

bullets.v: Stablecoin payments, passkey smart wallets and Soroban contracts.
New users in USDC, every sale on chain, and demand for a naira anchor.
